title: Priority Harmonization Gate for Strategic Escalations and Scoped SLAs
creator: Marcus Li
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers continue to surface high-severity roadmap requests via ad-hoc channels. PM and Eng are spending disproportionate time negotiating scope and commitments without a consistent decision gate. We need a deterministic mechanism that harmonizes signals (revenue, renewal risk, technical feasibility, compliance) into a single decision gate and a scoped SLA template for accepted escalations.

Objective: Build a Priority Harmonization Gate (PHG) — a lightweight intake + scoring + SLA generator + admin override flow that: 1) standardizes triage, 2) surfaces clear acceptance criteria to customers, and 3) produces a scoped SLA and execution runway when requests are accepted into a prioritized lane.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement billing changes, nor full automation of contract amendments. It also does not change Dedicated/Private onboarding flows beyond informing stakeholders.
acceptance_criteria: Intake API and web form capture standardized signals: account TCV, renewal date, escalation reason, reproducible impact, legal/compliance tags
Scoring engine computes a numeric harmonized priority score combining revenue, renewal risk, severity, and engineering effort estimate
Admin UI shows top-5 signals, computed score, and recommended lane (Fast-track / Standard / Defer)
When accepted, system generates a scoped SLA draft (scope, timeline, rollback/fallback) and files a follow-up PM/Eng playbook link
Manual override allowed with required justification and audit log entry
Telemetry: dashboard with weekly volume, median time-to-decision, and % of accepted items meeting projected runway
deliverables: Open intake form (Console + Intake API) with required fields
Priority Harmonization scoring service prototype (rules + weights)
Admin decision UI wireframes and working frontend for reviewers
Scoped SLA templating engine and generated draft output
Runbook for PM/SE handoff after acceptance
Dashboard tile in Console showing PHG metrics
approach: Phase 1: Lightweight MVP that uses rules-based scoring (no ML) to align stakeholders quickly. Use existing account metadata in CRM to enrich submissions. Phase 2: Iterate weights after two cycles and add automation for SLA acceptance emails. Phase 3: Explore stochastic forecasting to predict runway slippage and auto-suggest mitigations.

risks: Misweighted scoring could bias decisions toward revenue only, disadvantaging high-risk security requests
Customer expectations may exceed the scope of a generated SLA draft; legal must sign off before any commitment
Engineering capacity constraints could lead to accepted items being reclassified and damage trust
Data gaps in CRM (missing renewal dates) will reduce scoring accuracy
open_questions: Should account advocacy notes from Sales count as a weighted input? (Sales Ops opinion required)
What is the escape hatch for urgent security issues that need immediate engineering attention?
How granular should the SLA templates be for Dedicated vs Hosted customers?
Do we need an explicit finance approval step for items tied to TCV > $250k?
rollout_plan: Start with a 2-week internal alpha using 3 chosen accounts; run weekly syncs with Sales and Support. Collect decision logs and adjust weights after the first 10 items. Expand to a 6-account pilot after stabilization, then release as opt-in Console feature for Enterprise tenants in release console-2025.03.
notes: This ticket intentionally separates the decision gating mechanics from contractual execution. Legal ownership of final SLA signatures remains outside scope; the system will only produce draft artifacts and audit trails. Engage Legal early for templating to avoid rework.
